newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ECONOMIC GROWTH SUSTAINABLE, NAM SAYS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ECONOMIC GROWTH SUSTAINABLE, NAM SAYS.

text.p: The U.S. economy will continue to expand at a healthy pace while inflation should remain subdued, the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) said in a report on Thursday.

"The growth rate for 1998 is projected at 2.6 percent, with inflation at 2 percent," the report said. "The exceptionally low inflation rates make it likely that the expansion will be sustained for the foreseeable future."
NAM said the unbridled expansion reflected strong gains in productivity, fueled by innovation and technological advances.

In its short-term forecast for the U.S. economy, NAM said it expected growth to pick up temporarily from the 2.2 percent reported for the April-June quarter, citing an expected rebound in consumer spending on the back of strong employment, income and wealth gains.
"However, by the fourth (quarter) the economy settles back to a more sustainable pace," NAM said.

The report said fiercer competition was the key reason for continuing low rates of inflation, while stable monetary and fiscal policies had also contributed. "The major reason for low inflation is greater competition at all levels," it said.
